P.W.1 escaped after being taken by some college boys to a different location, from where she fled to the CBS Bus Stand. A formal complaint was then filed on her behalf by P.W.2 and she was sent for medical examination to confirm her age and gather evidence of sexual exploitation. The police concluded investigation and filed charge sheet arraying A1 to A10. Case against A1 & A9 was split up. 6. The trial Court framed charges against A2 to A8 and A10 for the offence under Sections 366 and 506 IPC, Sections 3, 4 and 5 of Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act, 1956, A5 to A8 and A10 for the offence under Section 376(2)(g) IPC, A2 to A4 for the offence under Section 376(2)(g) r/w 109 IPC. 7.
texts.arguments: 8. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants argued that the testimony of PW1 contains numerous inconsistencies. On the other hand, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor argued on behalf of the State stating that hapless victim/P.W.1 was subjected to rape and she was forced to become a prostitute whereby A2 to A4 were the pimps and A5 to A8 had mercilessly raped her.

A5 to A8 are sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten years under Section 376(2)(g) IPC.
Learned Sessions Judge having considered the evidence on record convicted the appellants as stated supra while acquitting A10.
Further, the Sessions Judge found that as on the date of offence, victim girl was not a minor.
PW1's statement of intending to travel to Bangalore is implausible, as she has no known relations there.
Counsel further submits that if the brother of P.W.1, was selling chips at the bus stand, the police should have been able to locate him, yet the prosecution provided no explanation for his absence.
The owner of the house where PW1 was allegedly kept was not called to testify.
PW1's age certificate could have been obtained from her school, as she had studied up to the 10th class.
No test identification parade was conducted for PW1 to identify the appellants.
The appellant's surname is missing in Exhibit P8.
In the said circumstances, appellants conviction is proper.
10. Having gone through the record, learned Sessions Judge has correctly found that the victim was not a minor when the incident has taken place.

11. The allegation of committing gang rape by A5 to A8 at the instance of A2 to A4 is on the basis of testimony of P.W.1 who stated that when P.W.1 wanted to go to Bangalore, A2 to A4 asked her and informed that they would secure a room an

She was taken to Radhika Theater,
Sainagar, Kushaiguda where A5 to A8 and A10 raped her.
The other instance narrated by P.W.1 is that after considerable period of the alleged rape, the traffic police on Tankbund Police Station took her to the Police Station.
Then the police let her go after she paid some amount and then she returned to room near Radhika Theater and wanted to escape from A2 to A4.
However, her attempts to escape did not succeed and A2 to A4 beat her.

When she tried to escape from the police station,
one police constable had taken her and handed over to A2 to A4.
At the instance of A2to A4, A5 to A10 raped her.
12. The said two instances narrated by P.W.1 form basis for the learned Sessions Judge to record conviction for gang rape against A5 to A8 and abetting gang rape by A2 to A4.
13. The version of A10 that he was not present, was believed by the learned Sessions Judge and he was acquitted.
No reasons are given as to why the learned Sessions Judge has not believed P.W.1 selectively regarding rape by A10 and accepted the version of P.W.1 that she was raped by A5 to A8.
It is not in dispute that the police failed to identify the place of the alleged rape which was in a room near Radhika Theater.
P.W.1 has not shown the place where the alleged gang rape had taken place.
14. According to P.W.1, she was in Hyderabad till the date of lodging complaint on 28.09.2006.
In her examination in chief before the Court below her date of birth is not given nor the approximate year was stated though she studied till 10th class and stayed in a hostel at Hyderabad.

Thereafter,
her brother wanted to take her to Bangalore and took her to Railway Station and left her there stating that he would get food but did not return.
Then A2 to A4 came there and took her to room at Kushaiguda.
15. According to the complaint Ex.P1, P.W.1 came to Hyderabad in December, 2005 and the alleged luring by A2 to A4 was in December, 2005.

What happened from December, 2005 to December,
2006 was not specifically stated in the complaint.
However, narration is given that A2 to A4 were bringing customers and she was catering to the customers.
Even in the complaint Ex.P1, it is no where stated as to when A5 to A8 committed gang rape.
Learned Sessions Judge, while discussing the evidence noted that there was lack of evidence against A5 to A8 and also against A10 regarding sexual acts with P.W.1.
However, it does not affect the case of gang rape.
As already stated A10 was acquitted by disbelieving the evidence of P.W.1 that A10 also raped her along with A5 to A8.
